body:
Ive been self-medicating for about 25 years to manage what I later discovered in my late 30s was undiagnosed ADHD. The most effective treatment for me has always been full-psychedelic doses of psilocybin mushrooms. A long walk alone in nature with a dramatic ego-death experience seems to "defragment" my mind and keeps me stable for at least six months. However, as Ive gotten older, it takes a lot more effort to psych myself up for these trips. While theyre amazing, they can also be quite exhausting.
So, I started looking for other options to help fill the gaps between those trips, especially for moments of crisislike during the winter when my thoughts tend to spiral into dark places. Ive read a lot of scientific papers about mind-altering substances, and ketamine caught my attention. Unfortunately, its hard to find trustworthy sources for it. Thats when I came across deoxymethoxetamine (DMXE), a novel ketamine analogue with a slightly longer duration of action. There isnt much research on it yetjust a few papers mostly focusing on its NMDA receptor affinity. One study showing disturbing brain scans of chronic ketamine users reminded me to proceed with caution. I also read all the user reports I could find before trying it myself.
For my trial, I bought two gray pellets from a Dutch manufacturer, each containing 40 mg of DMXE.
The Trial
After a week of reading and preparation, I decided to carefully try a dissociative for the first time. I figured a quarter of a pellet (10 mg) taken intranasally would be a reasonable starting pointunlikely to harm my brain or be dangerous. I crushed a piece of the pill and sniffed it in one go. No burning, just a slight pharmaceutical sting and a faint smell/flavor that reminded me a bit of cocaine.
+5 minutes:
I feel something happeninga subtle numbness in my nose.
+15 minutes:
Im feeling tipsy but calm. I keep observing myself, but there are no signs of any physical or mental discomfort.
+30 minutes:
I feel so relaxed and at peace. I decide to add another 10 mg.
+60 minutes:
The second dose kicks in gently, building on the first. The feeling is unlike anything Ive experienced before. Im trying to analyze this state but cant quite pin it down. I open my laptop and start searching for music on YouTube. Typically, I lean towards ambient artists like Tim Hecker, Biosphere, or Boards of Canada when on psychedelics. For some reason, YouTube suggests Led Zeppelin. Id never been much of a fan, but I decided to give Stairway to Heaven (live) a try.
The first notes felt like they were caressing my soul. I melted into the music. Every tone seemed to pull on a string directly attached to a blissful non-existence. It was one of the best musical experiences of my life. I smiled and giggled, completely absorbed, savoring every second of it.
When the song ended, I realized the drugs effects were quite pronounced. I had completely lost myself in the music for a while. Feeling thirsty, I got up to grab some water, but walking felt like Id had a couple of beerslight-headed but steady. In the kitchen, I kept forgetting why I was there. It was hard to focus on my intentions, but I didnt feel frustrated about it. Eventually, I managed to drink a glass of water and return to the music. I spent the rest of the evening listening to various genres, astonished and completely absorbed.
+23 hours:
The effects gradually faded, leaving me in a calm, relaxed mood. I felt pleasantly tired but struggled to fall asleep, so I took 0.5 mg of melatonin. That did the trick, and I was asleep within 30 minutes.
The Aftermath
In the days that followed, I noticed no sign of depression. My usual habit of having two beers to unwind in the evening disappeared. I just felt fine. That said, I did notice a mild craving to try DMXE againnot an overwhelming urge, but Id be lying if I said I wasnt tempted. I plan to wait a week or two before revisiting that "zen state."
Heres the most surprising takeaway: DMXE seemed to turn off my "Radio ADHD." The constant inner dialogue, parallel chains of thoughts, fantasies, and overthinkingall of it was gone for a while. It felt almost too good to be true. Ill definitely proceed with caution because this stuff is powerful.
